I always said that I was elected to the post of the first vice-president. Therefore, there is a mistake in the records quite obviously. And I say that under oath, and you have the tape, the audiotape of what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure if I have it. I won't debate it with you. That's why I'm clarifying the issue with you. I just want to know which one it was. That's all. Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, with respect to your position as first vice-president of the SDA in 1990, can you tell us when you were removed, replaced, or discharged from that position as first vice-president of the SDA?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I was replaced from that post, that took place, I think, in 1996, but I'm not quite sure. After the war at any rate, after the period that we're discussing.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So if a witness who happened to have been also a first vice-president of the SDA during the time in which you were in November of 1990, if he were to suggest to this Court that both you and he were replaced as the first vice-presidents of the SDA in November of 1991, he would be wrong or inaccurate. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not correct. Throughout that time, I held the post of first vice-president. And I remember that very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If I may, Your Honour, just go into private session to ask about the name of the individual, although I do not believe that he had a pseudonym, I just want for all purposes of caution not to ask him to identify the individual now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Confirmed. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Sejmenovic. With respect to the SDA, from 1990, were you also a member of the Executive Board?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From 1990, I was a member of the Executive Board, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And from when to when were you a member of the SDA Executive Board?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't give you the exact dates. I don't remember when the elections within the party took place exactly. But I don't think I was a member of the Executive Board later on, after that. But by virtue of my function as a member of the republican parliament, I did attend the meetings of the Executive Board of our party.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I understand that, and we'll get to it. Thank you. Do you recall at all if you remained a member of the SDA Executive Board at any time prior to April 1992, or any time from January to April 1992?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I was, before that period. That is to say, before being elected in the party, the first regular elections in the party.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: My question perhaps was inaccurate. Please, just a little clarification on that. The elections for the party were November 1990. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: The same time that the multiparty elections for Bosnia and Herzegovina were. Correct? Approximately.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately at that time, yes. But they were elections which were held from the initiative boards and from the structures of the initiative boards of the party. Later on, the first, as we called them, the first normal, regular elections took place within the party itself, and that is where certain changes took place.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Help me with this, if you can: Do you know the reasons why you were removed from the Executive Board of the SDA?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At these elections, the first regular elections within the party, some people nominated me as a candidate for the party president. I did not think that I should assume that position, and I did not agree with this nomination. Besides, some people wanted to put me on the list, but I gave up my own nomination publicly at that session. So officially, I was not a candidate. It is possible that during the voting, some people did vote me. I remember that some people contested that, against my own free will. Eventually, I just kept my position as a delegate, but if I remember correctly, I was no longer a member of the Executive Board. But I can't state that with absolute certainty because my memory is finite, after all.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If I can move on to another topic that's related to your testimony, you briefly shared with us the issue of pre-election negotiations between the SDA and the SDS. Do you recall generally that topic?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before the elections, are you referring to the period before the elections, the contacts with the SDS? Yes, I did speak about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Just wanted to put it in context. With respect to those pre-election negotiations, did you have any meetings with representatives from the SDS in connection with establishing a joint party platform or parties platform for the upcoming elections in November of 1990?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had several contacts, all with the same aim.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me what that aim was, sir?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Our ambition and our proposal to the steering committee of the SDS, I'm talking about the steering bodies on the basis of which parties were later registered. Our ambition and our intention and our request was to create a common election platform, a joint election platform. We proposed to have mass rallies together as a group of parties, an association of parties. We proposed to come forward jointly in terms of marketing also. We had several discussions on this, both in groups and individually.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And were the common or joint platforms agreed upon between the SDA and the SDS prior to November of 1990?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The SDS refused any intense form of cooperation in that respect. They refused to have joint rallies in the pre-election period. At first, this was generally accepted, and we did hold a number of joint meetings with our voters, those of the SDA and the SDS. I know of at least two cases, one of which I took part in myself. But after these first two joint events, the SDS gave up. The SDS kept on saying publicly that we needed to have some sort of cooperation, and our proposal to at least do our marketing jointly was accepted by the SDS. The only thing that was accepted was the idea that the SDA, the SDS, and the HDZ should have a common pre-election poster in order to show the voters that everybody was working for the same changes in the same direction and in order to prevent people from galvanizing and to show that we were sharing the same political platform and it was possible to reach an agreement, even in the pre-election period. Eventually, this part of our agreement was partly carried out, but not in full.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me what the platform of the SDA was prior to November of 1990, sir.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Our platform prior to November, that is, before the 1990 elections, was to topple communism and to democratise the society in Bosnia and Herzegovina. We wanted democratic changes to take place in Bosnia and Herzegovina. We wanted a multiparty system in place. This we saw as our most important goal. Even emotionally, that was the goal we worked towards. It was our top priority. We offered cooperation and requested cooperation from all other noncommunist parties, nonradical parties, and parties that were not of radical nationalistic orientation.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Is it true, sir, that, in fact, it was also the platform of the SDS prior to November 1990, and it was that platform that you just described that you earlier spoke of as being the "common joint platform" between the parties. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Verbally, yes. But not in any practical sense.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Help me with this: My question earlier was whether, or if you can share with us, what the SDA platform was, not what the joint common platform was. I'd like to know prior to 1990, what was the SDA platform in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already answered, that what the SDA platform was.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me if at any time prior to November 1990 elections, whether the SDA ever contemplated seeking sovereignty or independence for the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. At that time, I wasn't familiar with any such thing, nor have I ever heard anything about that. That sort of initiative first came up, or such statements, only after the events -- only after events took place at the federal level, after the other republics decided to opt for independence. That's when the issue was first raised. And the SDA saw as its priority task to fight for the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We'll get to that, hopefully, a little later. But just so the record is clear, that separation by other republics who were part of the former Yugoslavia occurred actually sometime from November through December of 1991. Correct, one year after the elections? Right?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I've already said, concerning Yugoslavia, both in our platform and on the common poster that I've referred to, bearing in mind the motives of the SDS and bearing in mind the possibility that the SDA proposed to have some form of Yugoslavia preserved in this common pre-election poster, we had the name "Yugoslavia" written on it. We did not rule out that possibility because a possibility is what we are talking about. But we did not know which course events would take. What became obvious at a later stage, the SDA did not want Bosnia and Herzegovina to become part of Serbia and Montenegro.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We'll get to all those issues later, sir. My only question is: Is it fair to state that at any time prior to November 1990, the SDA party never voiced privately or publicly any desire to separate, become independent, or to create a sovereign country within Bosnia and Herzegovina? Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The president of the SDA at that time proposed a way to save, to preserve, Yugoslavia together with the president of Macedonia. And here, he was a spokesman of SDA policies. And there were several initiatives at that point to save, preserve, Yugoslavia. Later developments went in a completely opposite direction. If you wish to ask me whether within the SDA, for no reason at all someone said "let's go and fight against Yugoslavia, let's go and secede" I have never heard anything like that said. And I am not familiar that anyone was representing that view in the SDA.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, I'm not arguing with you. All I wanted to -- and I think you've answered the question, so I'm going to move on to the issue of posters that you discussed. We'll get to 1991. With respect to 1990, I think your evidence is clear that no one from the SDA, correct me if I am wrong, sought either publicly or privately the independence or sovereignty of Bosnia and Herzegovina. 1990, we're talking about.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I've said, this didn't happen at the time the SDA was established. So when the steering committees were still the essence of the whole process, it didn't happen at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll get to the time when it happened a little later. But right now, that was the point of the question. With respect to the posters that were being created prior to the elections of November 1990, you participated, I believe your testimony was, in at least one meeting, but correct me if I am wrong, in connection with this joint platform or an attempt to make a coalition between the three parties, the HDZ, SDA, and SDS. Were those meetings that were attended by leaders of each of those three representative political groups?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I myself attended one meeting. That's if we're talking about the joint electoral meetings. Another meeting was attended by a local official, Franke [phoen], not from the municipal level. I think from the area of Cele or Gomjenica. His name was Mesic Muhamed. He managed to organise, at his own local level, a joint meeting of the leaders of the SDS and the SDA. And also, an opportunity to address Serb voters. Of course, they were also invited to meetings where voters of other nationalities, that's Bosniak, Muslim nationalities, were addressed.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me if, during the meeting in which you participated, involving the issue of the posters who were present on behalf the SDS?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the meeting where we spoke about the final version of the poster, this meeting was held in a hotel in Prijedor immediately following the meeting of the municipal board of the SDS, or the steering committee of the SDS. So that meeting had already been underway. We were told to come at a certain time. I came with two assistants. We brought proposals for the poster, and we had a discussion. There were many people in the room, because there had been a meeting in that room previously. I know that the president, Srdjo Srdic, did not attend that meeting, but Dr. Kovacevic was there. So was Dragan Savanovic. Other people were there, too. But I can't remember who.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, isn't it true that Dr. Milomir Stakic was not at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember. I can neither confirm nor deny this.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Let me switch to another -- if I may switch to another topic, sir. Now we're moving to the election of 1990. You shared with us testimony on June 12th, 2002, that you were elected as a member of the Chamber of Municipalities for the Prijedor municipality. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: On page 17 of your transcript on line 4, question was asked as follows: "The Marko Pavic was another candidate who seemed to be a candidate for a number of people. There was no candidate there for the SDS party." Answer, commencing on line 7 of page 17 of Wednesday, June 12th, 2002 transcript as follows: "The SDS party did not have a candidate for this chamber. At least, in the Prijedor municipality. And they decided to support Marko Pavic, who was a candidate of the coalition of left-wing parties which were descendants of the former League of Communists." I'll continue to read the rest of it for the Court and for the record. Continuing with the quote: "There was never made public as a formal position of the party; however, the fact remains that the party did not offer its candidate for this seat. And the fact that Marko Pavic received this number of votes proves that the SDS has chosen him as their Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. candidate. And in the first round, nobody won the necessary per cent. That was the reason why we had a second round. And I won a sufficient number of votes during that second round and received a seat in the republic parliament." End quote at line 17.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The necessary 51 per cent.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. I thought that was the line. "The necessary 51 per cent." There's no dispute about that. With the Court's permission, the usher to hand Exhibit S131A -- I think it's page 39 of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: While they are looking for that, Mr. Sejmenovic, I'm going to ask you a question in connection with your testimony that I just read, or parts of it obviously, and this document S131. So if you would be kind enough to tell me when you've had an opportunity to review that, and what I'm looking for is, specifically, that page 39 relating to the chamber of municipalities' election results for the Prijedor municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If I may, Your Honour, I think we used the English version on page 39, but he's welcome to look at either one.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Just so that we're following along, there's a paragraph numbered 74, which is in capital letters, states "the constituency of the municipality of Prijedor." Correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Then it goes on to indicate the number of voters that were registered and the actual number of voters that cast ballots. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, this Marko Pavic that is mentioned that election for the municipality of Prijedor, he was with what party?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here it reads that he was a candidate of the League of Communists of the -- the Democratic Union of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the Socialist Youth Association, Democratic Association of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the Association of Democratic Forces for Bosnia and Herzegovina, and the Party of Private Initiative for Bosnia and Herzegovina. This is the bloc that I was referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, in your testimony as I earlier stated, last Wednesday, June 12th, you stated on line 7: "The SDS party did not have a candidate for this chamber, at least in the Prijedor municipality, and they decided to support Marko Pavic." My question to you, sir, immediately underneath Marko Pavic's name and immediately above your name on subparagraph 3, is there a list of a candidate who appears for the seat of the chamber of municipalities for the municipality of Prijedor relating to the November of 1990 elections?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Number 2, it reads Stojan Vracar, a Serb, from Nisevici, candidate of the Serbian Democratic Party of Bosnia and Herzegovina." That's how this reads. But Stojan Vracar was a member of the radical party, of the Serbian Radical Party.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Is it your testimony, sir, that this document, then, is inaccurate? Wrong?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am merely contending that it is common knowledge that Stojan Vracar was an official of the Serbian Radical Party in Prijedor. That's what I contend.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Help me with this then: Is this document correct and accurate?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The document may be accurate only in as far as the Serbian Democratic Party had an agreement with the Serbian Radical Party to borrow their candidate. The document can only be accurate in that sense. Officially, the SDS nominated a person from a different party as their own candidate.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Whatever the case may be, whether the SDS took a candidate from another party or proposed a candidate from within their party, your testimony under oath to this Trial Chamber on June 12th, 2002, plainly stated that the SDS did not have a candidate for this party. Now, you tell me, sir, which is accurate?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The SDS did not have a candidate from their own ranks, not from their own members. Stojan Vracar was one of the founding members and one of the officials of the Serbian Radical Party. I am certain about that, and that's what I have always stated.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Let's look at how the first election and the results of that election. There were three -- regardless of who the person is. There were three people who participated in that election. According to this document, SDP party representative, an SDS party representative, again, respectfully, understanding your testimony that you just shared with us, and yourself, sir, from the SDA. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: It states here that you are from Sarajevo. Is that wrong also? Does that mean, sir, that you are a candidate from the headquarters of the SDA in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That's not what this says. This doesn't say that I'm from Sarajevo. This only gives my name, my last name, candidate of the SDA in Sarajevo. So the party was registered in Sarajevo for the whole of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: That's what I wanted to ask you. SDA Sarajevo is an indication that that's the central headquarters or the place of the party registration, in Sarajevo. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The party was registered and founded in Sarajevo. However, it was registered locally also in all municipalities where branches of the party were set up.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Marko Pavic received, on the first round of the elections, 17.271 votes. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember the precise numbers, but I suppose that's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: As you're sitting here today, is there any reason that you have that you would doubt the numbers that are printed in the document that's been offered by the Office of the Prosecution for this Tribunal to understand, digest, and accept?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, but typos do occur here and there in these documents. So I can't say whether there are any typos here or not, typing errors. You asked me about the SDA Sarajevo. In all the other news here, you can see the SDA without the Sarajevo part. I've just checked some other municipalities now, candidate of the SDA, but without the addition "Sarajevo." Here it does says "Sarajevo." Whoever typed this, what they added and whatnot, it is not up to me to ascertain that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: As you sit here, sir, do you know how many votes you received in November of 1990? Maybe that will help with the line of questioning that I'm asking.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the first round of the elections.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here it says 21.073 votes, but I didn't memorize that. It would have been pointless obviously for me to memorize exactly how many people had voted. I knew I couldn't go through to the next round, so we had to repeat this.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I wouldn't expect you to remember that, sir. But my question is for the purposes of our discussion on this issue, can we agree to rely at least on these numbers, or would you rather not?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the figures are accurate. This is an official gazette. I can't see why anyone would make up figures.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you this question: You testified under oath last Wednesday, June 12th, 2002 that at the runoff elections, the SDS party supported the other candidate, Mr. Marko Pavic. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said, according to the results, we had the impression that the SDS had backed another candidate. It was common knowledge in Prijedor that the SDS had not nominated any other candidate for that position. There was only Stojan Vracar, official of the Serbian Radical Party on the list. How this nomination reached the republic committee, we didn't know. But on the ground, we all knew that. And candidates were officially presented both on the radio and in newspaper interviews. That's how Stojan Vracar was presented, too. He never said "I'm a member of the SDS."

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us to the best of your recollection, with respect to Mr. Stojan Vracar, as it's stated here, he received 16.957 votes. Do you think, sir, that the votes came from party membership representative from the SDA party, the SDP party, or the SDS party?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Came to whom, from where? Who do you mean? We have three candidates here.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Of the votes that were cast, the 55.000-plus votes that were cast, the votes that Mr. Stojan Vracar got 16.900 plus votes, who were his constituents? Exclusively the radical party? The SDS party? Or any other number of parties that you can identify?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The electorate, the voters voted. I didn't ask them. We had the results, and that was it. And it was a secret ballot in every sense of the word.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: How do you, sir, then tell this Court that, as a result of the runoff, when you received an additional approximately 3.000 votes and the candidate that you ran against also received approximately or received approximately an additional 4.000 votes, Marko Pavic, how can you tell this Court, on line 12 page 17: "And the fact that Marko Pavic received this number of votes proves that the SDS has chosen him as their candidate"? In fact, sir, isn't it true that if you add the votes that you received and the votes that Mr. Marko Pavic received in the second runoff, fewer people voted than they did in the first election?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't calculate that. I didn't add it up. If you want me to do so, I can do so now.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: You received 51 per cent of vote, did you not?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: You received 24.000 votes. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Somewhere thereabouts, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Who got the other 49.17 per cent of the votes?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Marko Pavic did, the opposing candidate. There was no other choice. There was the second runoff, there were two candidates who had the most number of votes in the first round, and then the voting took place, and we had the result that we see.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: It's necessary to have at least a very short break, until 6.20.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honours, lead counsel Ms. Korner will be absent for a few minutes. She is in Courtroom I in the Brdjanin/Talic trial, trying to resolve this issue of timing on Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Nevertheless, we may proceed with the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Sejmenovic. Moving along from Document S131A and B, I'd like to ask you a series of questions now. So we can actually put that document away. I don't think we'll need it for the next series of questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'd ask the Court to ask the usher to kindly remove it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: As you stated, sir, you won the election runoff in November of 1990 and became a member of the chamber of municipalities from the Prijedor Municipality. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Upon being an elected member, were you required to take an oath of office?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, all members of parliament took an oath of office.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Help me with this, Mr. Sejmenovic: Did you take an oath of office? I'm not right now interested in the other members. All I want to know is if you did, yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody took the oath individually. 240 members of parliament took the oath at the same time. That's what I'm saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'd like to know whether you took the oath of office, following your election in November 1990.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I've already said, just like all the rest, I took the oath of office together with all the others.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'm not disputing that the other people took the office, but I'm just curious to know what you know and to share with us your experiences. So limit your answers, if you will, to the question that I am asking in connection with you, personally.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already answered your question. I did take the oath of office.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, please, whether or not the oath of office sought that you express loyalty to the former Yugoslavia and the constitutions and laws under which the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina were a part in November of 1990?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember the actual text of the oath itself, the wording.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If I may, I'd like now, sir, to direct your attention to your June 11th, 2002, written witness statement given to the ICTY.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And if I may ask the Court if the usher can just take the document for verification of signature, I want to just have a complete record and show it to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sejmenovic, did you have an opportunity to review the document dated June 11, 2002, which is a witness statement given by you before the ICTY?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have before me the English version. May I please have the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I do have the B/C/S version, Your Honour, but it goes to the signature just that's reflected. But I'd be happy to give it to the usher, if she would be kind enough to help us here.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have looked through the statement, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Does your name, sir, appear anywhere on the B/C/S version of this statement dated May 29th and June 11th, 2002?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, my name is mentioned, and I gave the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. My question was inartful. I apologise. Does your signature appear on the B/C/S version of that document dated May 29th and June 11th, 2002?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My signature does not exist on the B/C/S version. You'll find my signature on the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And that's truly all I'm trying to establish. Is that your signature that appears on page 1 of the English translation of your statement May 29th and June 11th, 2002?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And those are your initials that appear on pages 2, 3, and 4 of that document. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. They are my initials.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And again on page 5, your signature appears, correct, with the date of 11th of June, 2002? Correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: With respect to this document, sir, it states on page 2, paragraph 2, line 2. For the convenience of the record I suppose and the Court, obviously, I'll read the paragraph in its entirety: "Between the 28th and 30th May, 2002, I attended the office of the Prosecutor of the ICTY in The Hague. There, I viewed numerous documents relevant to the trial of Milomir Stakic. I also viewed a video which featured myself in an interview given in 1992 when I was detained in Omarska camp. In relation to my knowledge of Milomir Stakic and events relevant to him in 1992, I can state the following..." Focussing our attention just for the moment on this paragraph, number 2 on page 2, and specifically the second sentence of that paragraph it states again: "There, I viewed numerous documents relevant to the trial of Milomir Stakic." Can you describe for us, sir, what those numerous documents were that you reviewed two weeks prior to your testimony here today or this week?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I did not make my own notes with respect to the documents that were shown me. Part of those documents I saw here. They were placed at my disposal to look through them and to give my comments in the course of this trial. I do not have a record of the documents that were -- which they were, but I know that some documents from the Crisis Staff in Prijedor were shown me as well as a police report, a party report, et cetera. I did not endeavour to remember them, nor did I keep records of the documents. But I did see the documents while during the procedure preparing witnesses for trial. I saw that in the office of the OTP and the investigating team. And I recognise some of the documents here in court when they were presented in the form of material.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, sir, if you remember, approximately two weeks ago, whether or not you reviewed the fourth amended revised indictment, as it relates to Dr. Stakic?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you, sir, review any of the transcripts of witnesses who testified before this Court prior to your testimony?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you review any such summaries of those witnesses?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you review any ICTY written statements from other witnesses other than the statement that you have shared with us today? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I know your testimony dealt a lot with the SDS party, and we'll talk about that in short order. Did you, in preparation for your testimony for this matter, review any documents relating to the SDA party, whether it be the Executive Board or its regular party membership meetings from the period of November 1990 up and through April of 1992?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, I did not review any documents whatsoever. I received an invitation to appear in court, and I received it at a late date. I had very -- a very short period of time to come. I spent last week here, the preparations lasted for several days. Then I went back. I tried to get through the business that I had to leave behind, and I was told once again that I had to come here, and it was not a timely invitation. And I came here, and worked for some time with the investigator. I neither had time nor, to tell you the truth, am I used to this kind of thing, or would I be interested in reviewing documents of that kind. This is an additional burden on me, in addition to all my general daily affairs and business. And I have to invest great effort to respond to the matters you're interested in here.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And I understand, sir, and we appreciate your patience, especially as it relates to my questions. So to follow up, is it then incorrect that indeed, as it states on page 2, paragraph 2, sentence 2 of your statement which you signed: "There, I viewed numerous documents relevant to the trial of Milomir Stakic"?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is correct, but I cannot tell you the number. That's what I was referring to. So the Prosecutor did show me a certain number of documents which I reviewed.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And I understand that, and thank you for that. I want to see if the documents -- strike that. I would like to know if you reviewed any documents relating to the Municipal Assembly minutes prior to April of 1992?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that I was shown a particular minutes, but I didn't look through it in any great detail because I didn't have any questions that arose thereof. So I just looked through it for the purposes of informing myself, and I looked at some sections in no particular order or just glancing here and there.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did the office of the Prosecutor, by chance, have you review the Territorial Defence list of weapons and members from the Kozara or Trnopolje area?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Prosecutor showed me parts of those lists, and they were shown me in the Tadic and Kovacevic cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And that was a three-page document which has your name and signature, which appears on the third page under line item 106. Correct? That's the document you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Fair enough. Did they share with you or show you, meaning the office of the Prosecutor, minutes of meetings held by the Territorial Defence members of Kozara during the year of 1992?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember having been shown anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you remember being shown, sir, a military report compiled on 17 November, 1993, in the Bosnia-Herzegovina embassy in Zagreb? Did you review that report at all?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that was not shown me.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know who a gentleman by the name of Senad Kubat is?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know Senad Kubat. He was one of the SDA officials in Bosanska Gradiska Municipality. And for a while in 1993, 1994, I'm not sure, he was an official either of the consulate of Bosnia and Herzegovina in Zagreb or in a related department. I don't know what the department was in a legal sense, but I know he worked there briefly, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you share with us how well you knew him?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew him by sight.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether -- or can you give an opinion as to Mr. Senad Kubat's veracity, truthfulness, honesty, and integrity? Would you know anything about those things with respect to Mr. Kubat?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't answer that question. He was just a common man. He liked to drink sometimes, to have a drop too many even. That may have been a slightly bad thing about him. It was like that for a while. I don't know whether he stopped later on. We did not socialise privately, so I can't speak about his essence as a man.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know a gentleman or -- strike that. Did you review a report or any documents from a person by the name of Jusuf Ramic?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I am not familiar.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: That was my second question. Did you know him?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Jusuf Ramic, no, not as far as I can remember now.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At least at this point in time I can't remember. I must have seen a thousand people, but had he been a prominent figure in this whole process, I probably could remember. But I can't remember him at this point.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time, I'd like with the Court's permission, to go into closed session pursuant to a discussion that the OTP and I had in connection with this next topic. And maybe we could share with you in closed session, and the Court can decide whichever...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Objections?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. If it's the topic we discussed, no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please, closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: 7.03 p.m., to be reconvened on Thursday, the 20th day of June, 2002, at 2.15 p.m.
